WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Amos 8:2 "‘The end has come for My people Israel'"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:2 "‘The end has come for My people Israel'" The VERB (BDB 97, KB 112, Qal PERFECT) denotes that the covenant between YHWH and Abraham's descendants will be abrogated with the northern tribes.

The pain of YHWH can be sensed in the covenant phrase, "My people Israel"( cf. Hosea 11:1-4,8), but it will not be completely abrogated. There is hope (cf. Amos 9:7-15; Hosea 11:9-11).

 To allow the appearance of the covenant to continue would be cruel. YHWH's judgment, as painful as it was, was an act of love with a real potential of restoration (cf. Amos 9:14-15)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "will spare them no longer" This phrase is very emphatic. Literally, it is "I will never (BDB 414, KB 418, Hiphil IMPERFECT) again pass by them" (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT).

The Covenant is broken (cf. Amos 7:8)! His people have rejected Him by their amalgamation with Canaanite fertility worship for the last time. In Gen. 15:16 the Amorites of the Promised Land were rejected because of their godless lifestyle. Now YHWH's own people are being turned out because of their similar godless lifestyle. God's patience coming to an end. This is clearly seen in Isa. 6:9-13; Jer. 15:5-9 and Ezek. 7:2-9.

8:3
NASB  "the songs of the palace"
NKJV, NRSV, Peshitta  "the songs of the temple"
REB, NJB  "the palace songs"
TEV  "the songs in the palace"
JPSOA  "the singing women of the palace"
LXX  "the ceilings of the temple shall howl"

The term "songs" (BDB 1010) is FEMININE PLURAL, which may denote the irony that the female singers (same Hebrew root revocalized) at court would become the professional mourners. But, there were so many bodies that the only sound was silence! (For a brief discussion of mourning rites see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 1, pp. 56-61.)

There is a possibility of two translations:

  1. "palace" (TEV, NJB, cf. Amos 6:5)
  2. "shrine" or "temple" (cf. Amos 5:23)

Because of Amos 8:10 (cf. Amos 5:23) option #2 seems best.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "will turn to wailing" The VERB (BDB 410, KB 413, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) occurs several times in the section of Jeremiah dealing with judgment on the surrounding nations (cf. Jer. 47:2; 48:20,31,39; 49:3; 51:8). He seems to follow Isaiah's usage (cf. Isa. 13:6; 14:31; 15:2,3; 16:7[twice]; 23:1,6,14). A good translation of this outcry over death and destruction could be "wail," "howl," "shriek."

The eighth century minor prophets used this imagery several times in relation to YHWH's coming judgment.

  1. Hosea 7:14
  2. Joel 1:5,11,13 (date unknown, possibly early post-exilic)
  3. Amos 8:3
  4. Micah 1:8

▣ "in that day" This was a standardized imagery for judgment used so often in the eighth century prophets. YHWH will visit His people for

  1. blessing (cf. Amos 9:11,13)
  2. cursing (cf. Amos 1:14; 2:16; 3:14; 4:2; 5:8,18,20; 6:3; 8:3,9,10,11,13)
  3. See full note at Amos 2:16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

▣ "they will cast them forth in silence" This refers to abnormal burial practices (i.e. no professional wailing nor any wailing at all) because of invasion and siege. This phrase is related to Amos 6:10 (the same INTERJECTION is used, BDB 245, "hush").

SPECIAL TOPIC: BURIAL PRACTICES

entries.title: Amos 8:4 "Hear"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:4 "Hear" This is the Hebrew term Shema (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE). It means "to hear so as to do." It is often used of prayer (cf. Deut. 6:4-6; Amos 3:1,13; 4:1; 5:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ Verse 4 refers to subjugation (i.e. "trample" or "crush" BDB 983, KB 1375, Qal PARTICIPLE) of the poor ("the needy" parallel to "the humble of the land" and "the helpless. . .the needy," cf. Amos 8:6) by the rich and politically powerful (cf. Amos 2:7; 5:11,12).

The JPSOA suggests an emendation to the MT of this verse, which reads, "who on every new moon devour the needy, and on every sabbath the humbled of the land" (i.e. vv. 4-5).

entries.title: Amos 8:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:5 The wealthy, powerful, and influential could not wait for the religious assemblies (i.e. "new moon," cf. Num. 28:11; 2 Kgs. 4:23 and "sabbath," cf. Exod. 31:13-17) to be over so they could instigate their illegal, improper, and unjust schemes toward the poor:

  1. to make the bushel smaller
  2. the shekel bigger
  3. use dishonest scales
  4. sell the husk of the wheat (those grain heads that fell in the dirt, BDB 655, or under-developed grain that fell through the sieve, cf. Amos 9:9) with the wheat

All of these refer to cheating the poor when they buy food (cf. Lev. 19:35-36; Deut. 25:13-16; Prov. 20:10).

The VERBS "sell" (BDB 991, KB 1404) and "open" (BDB 834, KB 986) are both COHORTATIVE. These merchants' desire to exploit is so strong that their actions are the commands of their own hearts.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, II

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES (metrology)

▣ "the new moon" This refers to the ancient custom of observing a religious holiday at the first of the month (cf. Num. 28:11; 2 Kgs. 4:23). Remember, the Jews went by the lunar calendar.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, II. D.

▣ "dishonest scales" This CONSTRUCT (BDB 24, 941) denotes unfair and dishonest commercial enterprises, especially against the poor (cf. Micah 6:10-11). YHWH hates this falsehood (cf. Prov. 11:1). It is never "business is business" with God or His people! Exploitation reveals a heart of self, greed, and fallenness.

entries.title: Amos 8:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:6 This verse gives an example of how poor people who could not buy food were forced to sell themselves or their family members into slavery (i.e. the rich Israeli family for a period of time; this does not refer to the Phoenician slave trade) for a small amount (i.e. "a pair of sandals," cf. Amos 2:6).

These wealthy merchants sank so low as to sell grain mixed with husk, dirt, pebbles, etc. With profits from these fraudulent sales they purchased more slaves! Therefore, the poor paid for the exploitation of the poor!

entries.title: Amos 8:7 "The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:7 "The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob" In Amos YHWH swears several times as a way to show that His words are true:

  1. "The Lord God has sworn by His holiness," Amos 4:2
  2. "The Lord God has sworn by Himself," Amos 6:8
  3. "The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob," Amos 8:7

This phrase has several possibilities:

  1. God's glory in the descendants of Jacob (cf. 1 Sam. 15:29). The TEV translates this as "The Lord, the God of Israel, has sworn"
  2. since no where else does God swear by another person, this may mean, "the Lord, of whom Israel is so proud, has sworn" (UBS, Handbook, p. 165)
  3. that the people of Jacob had become so permanently wicked that YHWH could swear by their settled condition (cf. Amos 6:8)

▣ "I will never forget any of their deeds" This is a very strong and emphatic statement.

  1. a HYPOTHETICAL PARTICLE, (אט)
  2. a Qal IMPERFECT VERB, "to forget" (BDB 1013, KB 1489)
  3. the NOUN "everlasting," "perpetuity" (BDB 664)

These exploitative merchants will answer for the crimes against both their covenant brothers and sisters and their covenant God!

entries.title: Amos 8:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:8 This question expects a "yes" answer. This verse is apparently using the imagery of

  1. an earthquake mentioned in Amos 1:1
  2. the destruction caused by the annual flooding of the Nile River in Egypt (cf. Amos 9:5; Jer. 46:7-8)

Because this VERB (BDB 176, KB 204, Niphal PERFECT with waw) is used to describe Jonah being driven from the presence of YHWH (cf. Jonah 2:4), it may be imagery for exile from the Promised Land (cf. Amos 9:1-4,5). This same word was used of YHWH driving the Canaanites out of the Promised Land, but now Israel is being removed for her sins and idolatry (cf. Gen. 15:12-21)!

▣
NASB  "the land quake"
NKJV, NJB, Peshitta  "the land not tremble"
NRSV  "the land tremble"
REB  "the earth quake"
TEV  "the earth will quake"
LXX  "the land be troubled"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 919, KB 1182, Qal IMERFECT) "quake." The term "land" (BDB 75) can refer to Palestine or the whole region (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH). The PRONOUN "it" in vv. 8b,c,d; 10e,f, refers back to "land."

Apparently Amos is using both the major earthquake and the annual floodiing of the Nile (i.e. flood imagery of destruction) as parallel, denoting Israel's judgment. This imagery may go back to the Song of Moses in Exod. 15, esp. v. 14 (also note 1 Sam. 14:15).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA

▣
NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, JPSOA  "the Nile"
NKJV  "the River"
LXX, Targums, Vulgate  "a river"
Peshitta  "a flooded river"

The MT has two forms.

  1. כאר ‒ like the light (line c, see imagery in v. 9)
  2. כיאור ‒ like the Nile (line e, cf. Amos 9:5)

The UBS Text Project, p. 293, suggests that both spellings refer to the Nile River. However, it gives "the Nile" a "C" rating (considerable doubt). "The light" (i.e. option #1) does not make sense in this verse, but it might in v. 9.

entries.title: Amos 8:9
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:9 This verse has been understood in several ways:

  1. eschatological language (i.e. "in that day") like Amos 5:18-20; Isa. 13:10; Joel 2:2; 3:15; Micah 3:6
  2. a reference to the plagues on Egypt, which form the basis of the curses of Deuteronomy 27-29
  3. a literal reference to an eclipse (cf. Amos 5:18-20)

In a sense the cosmic chaos of creation is recurring. The ideal setting of YHWH fellowshipping with mankind has again been disrupted. Nature is seen as being in chaos (cf. Rom. 8:19-22).

It is ironic that water can be for destruction (i.e. flood) or a symbol of God's blessing (cf. Amos 5:24). Mankind will experience one or the other! For an interesting discussion of the word "sea" see NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 461-466.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS

▣ "make the earth dark in broad daylight" This VERB (BDB 364, KB 361, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) refers to YHWH's action. It may reflect the plague of darkness in Egypt (cf. Exod. 10:21-22; Ps. 105:28). Here it refers to God bringing darkness, both literal (cf. Amos 5:8) and figurative (cf. Amos 8:11-12). Israel's light is darkened (cf. Jer. 13:16).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT

entries.title: Amos 8:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:10 This is a series of mourning rites (i.e. funeral songs, sackcloth, baldness) over YHWH's judgments of Israel's worship times. Their worship will be turned to bitter mourning, like the death of an only son (cf. Jer. 6:26; Zech. 12: 10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "baldness" Because of Israel's connection with the Canaanite fertility cults, this could refer to "shaving" (cf. Moab, Isa. 15:2; Jer. 48:37; Philistia, Jer. 47:5; and Phoenicia, Ezek. 27:31), which had cultic connotations (cf. Lev. 21:5).

But it could also refer to the pulling out of the hair of the head as a sign of mourning (cf. Micah 1:16; Ezek. 7:18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "a bitter day" This word (BDB 600) is used at the grief over a death (cf. Amos 5:16-17). They were expecting just the opposite (cf. Amos 5:18-20)! This is a veiled reference to "that day," "the day of the Lord." See note at Amos 2:16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

entries.title: Amos 8:11
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:11 This may be the OT origin of one part of Jesus' beatitudes (cf. Matt. 5:6) and possibly a reference to Matt. 4:4, where Jesus quotes Deut. 8:3. Israel thought she had all she needed, but what all of us really need is fellowship with God (i.e. based on the revelation of His word)! Oh, what a terrible famine (cf. v. 12d; 1 Sam. 3:1; 2 Chr. 15:3; Ps. 74:9; Lam. 2:9; Ezek. 7:26)!

entries.title: Amos 8:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:12 This shows a frantic but futile search for God. What shocking imagery! God has been seeking mankind in love, but there will come a day when they will not be able to find Him. Humans were created to need fellowship with God (cf. Gen. 1:26-27). Hell is the removal of the possibility of being with Him!

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

▣ "from sea to sea" For a speaker in Palestine, this would refer to the Mediterranean to the Dead Sea. It is not very far physically, but it signifies from one end of the country to the other.

entries.title: Amos 8:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:13 Even the young and strong will not be able to find God. Exhausted young people are imagery for YHWH's judgment (cf. Isa. 51:20).

8:14
NASB, JPSOA  "the guilt"
NKJV, NJB  "the sin"
NRSV, REB  "Ashimah"
TEV, Peshitta  "idols"
LXX  "the atonement"

This (BDB 79, KB 96) refers to

  1. the golden calves (cf. 1 Kgs. 12:28; Hosea 8:5-6; 10:5) set up at the cities of Dan and Bethel by Jeroboam I (922 B.C.). They were meant to rival the temple in Jerusalem as a worship site for YHWH. All of the kings of the northern tribes are condemned by the prophets because of these shrines.
  2. There is another possible understanding of this text based on the consonental Masoretic Text. It has the phrase, "the Ashima of Samaria" (cf. 2 Kgs. 17:30). If so, this then would refer to the female fertility goddess of Canaan or Syria (see NKJV, NJB footnotes, cf. 2 Kgs. 17:30).

Whichever reference is correct, it reflects the improper worship of the Northern Ten Tribes, Israel.

▣ "As the way of Beersheba lives" This is an unusual reference. Beersheba is a city located in southern Judah. It was referred to earlier in Amos 5:5. Possibly the journey itself or the route with its cultic associations or the term "way" is idiomatic of a ritual or teaching. Exactly how or what is involved in this idolatry is uncertain.

It is just possible that a geographical emphasis is what is referred to (i.e. Dan to Beersheba, cf. Jdg. 20:1; 1 Sam. 3:20), which would parallel Amos 8:12. These covenant people committed idolatry throughout the Promised Land, but now they will frantically seek for YHWH again throughout the land, but will not find Him!

There is another option:

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "the way"
TEV  "the god"
NJB  "the pilgrimage"
REB  "the sacred way"
LXX  "your god lives"
Peshitta  "the cult"
NET  "your beloved one"

The MT has "the way" (BDB 202). There seems to be a parallel between

  1. "As your god lives, Dan"
  2. "As your _______ lives, Beersheba"

The NET Bible, p. 1602, suggests that "the way" may refer to

  1. a pilgrimage route, cf. Amos 4:4-5; 5:4-5; 8:12
  2. a title for a local god ("your beloved," an emendation, cf. Amos 6:10)

entries.title: Amos 9:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:1 This refers to the destruction of a sacred worship site (i.e. altar, possibly at Bethel). The mechanism was the earthquake (cf. Amos 1:1; 8:7-10; 9:1,9). The Israelites were trusting in their covenant relationship with YHWH, but He rejected their amalgamated religious worship (cf. Amos 5:21-24; 8:10). Oh, the danger of eclectic worship!

▣ "Smite the capitals" The VERB (BDB 645, KB 697) is a Qal IMPERATIVE. This verse has two IMPERATIVES and a Qal IMPERFECT used as a JUSSIVE (i.e. "quake" BDB 950, KB 1271).

The term "capital" (BDB 499) refers to the carved (decorated) top of the support stone columns.

▣ "the thresholds" "Thresholds" (BDB 706) refers to the frame in which the door of the temple is mounted (cf. Isa. 6:4).

▣ "break them on the heads of them all" This is referring to the destruction of the worshipers by supernatural means, similar to Samson destroying the Philistine temple in Jdg. 16:23-30. Here the mechanism seems to have been a divinely timed and targeted earthquake.

▣ The last three lines of Amos 9:1 assert that no Israelite will ultimately escape YHWH's judgment (cf. Amos 9:2-3, LXX, Peshitta, NRSV, REB, NET). It is similar in meaning to Amos 5:19.

Prophetic literature is characterized by judgment passages being placed beside salvation passages. This chapter is a good example.

  1. Amos 9:1-10, judgment
  2. Amos 9:11-15, salvation

Both are true, but there are conditions/options based on YHWH's mercy and human faith/repentance. A remnant of national Israel will survive to accomplish YHWH's redemptive plan (i.e. a Davidic King)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (THREE SENSES)

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Amos 9:2 "Though they dig into Sheol"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:2 "Though they dig into Sheol" Sheol (BDB 982, e.g. Isa. 5:14; 14:9; 28:15,18; 38:10) refers to the holding place of the dead. It is described as being in the earth (i.e. dig). This is similar to people trying to hide in the caves in Isa. 2:10,19-21; Luke 23:30; and Rev. 6:15-16.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, I. B.

▣ "My hand" ("My sight," v. 3) SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "though they ascend to heaven" This is the spacial opposite of Sheol. The language of these verses (i.e. Amos 9:1-4) is reminiscent of Ps. 139:8. There is no where to hide from an angry YHWH (cf. Heb. 10:31)!

In this verse heaven may refer to the atmosphere above the earth (cf. Gen. 1:1,14-19,20) and not YHWH's throne (although Isa. 14:12-14 seems to merge the Jewish concept of the first heaven and the third heaven).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

entries.title: Amos 9:2-3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:2-3 These verses describe the futility of trying to escape from YHWH's judgment (e.g. Job 34:22; Jer. 23:24; Isa. 29:15). The imagery used is the same as in Ps. 139:8, 9-12 (also note Prov. 15:11).

entries.title: Amos 9:3 "the summit of Carmel"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:3 "the summit of Carmel" This may be dual imagery:

  1. this site had very thick vegetation (BDB 502 II) with many caves
  2. this was a traditional worship site (cf. 1 Kings 18)

▣ "though they conceal themselves from My sight on the floor of the sea" This is obviously imagery for sinful mankind's attempt to hide from God (cf. Job 34:21-22; Ps. 139:9-12; Isa. 2:19-20; Jer. 16:16-17; Hosea 10:8; Luke 23:30; Rev. 6:16).

The Israelites were a desert people. They were afraid of vast, deep water. The last place they would hide is the deep!

▣ "I will command the serpent and it will bite them" This is an allusion to the mythical sea monster, Leviathan (cf. Job 3:8; 41:1; Ps. 74:13-14; 104:26; Isa. 27:1) or Rahab (cf. Job 9:13; 26:12; Ps. 89:10; Isa. 51:9). Notice God commands (BDB 845, KB 1010, Piel IMPERFECT) the chaos monster.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SERPENT

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREAT RED DRAGON

entries.title: Amos 9:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:4 This is a shocking verse. YHWH's anger and judgment will pursue them even into exile. They will be herded like cattle into a foreign land, but even there death will await them! God will show no compassion (cf. Hosea 1:6; 2:4) because they are no longer His covenant people (cf. Hosea 1:9; 2:23). This verse reflects the consequences of breaking God's covenant (cf. Lev. 26, Deut. 28; esp. Amos 9:33).

▣ "I will set My eyes against them for evil and not for good" This is exactly opposite to the covenant promises! This same imagery and terminology occur several times in Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 21:10; 39:16; 44:11,27). It reflects the cursing and blessing sections of Leviticus 26 and especially Deuteronomy 27-29.

Notice that YHWH has the power to command actions outside of the Promised Land in the nations supposedly controlled by other gods (LXX, Deut. 32:8). These other gods (i.e. elohim; SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.) are helpless. They are non-existent and cannot stop YHWH's wrath!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

entries.title: Amos 9:5
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:5 This may be another reference to "the earthquake," Amos 1:1; 8:8-9; 9:1 (i.e. the land, like the Nile River, rises and falls).

▣ "Lord God of hosts" This title is found in Amos 3:13; 4:13; 5:14,16,27; 6:8,14 (i.e. "God of hosts").

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (Adon and Kurios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

entries.title: Amos 9:5-6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:5-6 This is the last of the three doxologies, hymns, or poems to YHWH as creator (cf. Amos 4:13 and 5:8-9).

entries.title: Amos 9:6
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:6 These are difficult-to-translate creation imagery. They speak of God as creator of heaven and earth (i.e. Elohim, cf. Gen. 1; Ps. 104). He is the controller of heavenly bodies and water, both salt and fresh (i.e. forces of nature).

It is possible to translate "vaulted dome" (BDB 8) as "storehouse" and if so, then Amos 9:6a refers to YHWH's dwelling place and Amos 9:6b refers to mankind's dwelling place, both of which are created by Him (cf. Amos 9:5a, 6d).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣
NASB, NRSV, REB  "His upper chambers"
NKJV  "His layers"
TEV  "his home"
NJB  "his mansions"
JPSOA  "His chambers"
LXX  "his ascent"
Peshitta  "his stories"
NEB  "his steps"

The MT has BDB 752, KB 613, which can mean

  1. steps (MT Ketiv and Qere)
  2. stories (NKJV)
  3. ascent (LXX)

BDB suggests #2 is meant here. The UBS Text Poject, p. 255, gives the Qere, "his steps," a "B" rating (some doubt). It implied "steps" to YHWH's heavenly temple. See John H. Walton, The Lost World of Genesis One, where he sees Genesis 1 as preparing YHWH's temple; very interesting!

▣ "The Lord is His name" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D. and SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

entries.title: Amos 9:7
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:7 Both the questions of Amos 9:7 expect a "yes" answer. Basically YHWH is depreciating the covenantal uniqueness of Israel. The one and only God (SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM) has led all nations to and from their current geographical locations (cf. LXX, Deut. 32:8; and possibly implied in Deut. 29:26). It must have been painful for Israel to be compared to Ethiopia, Philistia, and Syria. This is in sharp contrast to the election theology of Amos 3:2! Israel, like all nations, will answer for their sins!

▣ "Israel from the land of Egypt" This is a reference to the Exodus, which was the beginning of Israel as a nation.

▣ "Caphtor" This refers to the island of Crete (BDB 499), which may have been the ancestral home of the Philistines (sea people of the Aegean).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PHILISTINES

▣ "Kir" This (BDB 885 III) may refer to

  1. a part of Mesopotamia near Elam (cf. Isa. 21:2 and 22:6)
  2. a word which means "walls" (BDB 885 I, KB 1099) and stands for Nineveh (Kir means "city")
  3. a river, Kur, in northern Armenia
  4. a mountain range (el-Kaiyara) forming the northern boundary of Syria (cf. Anchor Bible Dictionary, vol. 4, p. 83)
  5. ABD, vol. 4, p., 83, mentions that the LXX and Vulgate connect it to Libya Cyrene, 2 Kgs. 16:9
  6. The LXX in Amos 9:7, translates it as "the deep" (or "pit"), (derogatory sarcasm)
  7. ABD, vol. 4, p. 83, suggests the MT is a textual error for an Arabic term referring to oases" in North Arabia

entries.title: Amos 9:7-8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:7-8 UBS, A Translator's Handbook on the Book of Amos, makes an interesting observation on the relationship between Amos 9:7 and 8. Verse 7 states very emphatically that Israel is not special, unique, or privileged, yet Amos 9:8 shows YHWH's special covenant care for her (cf. p. 181).

This same tension about God's covenant people exists in the New Testament.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "TENSIONS" (Excerpted from "Crucial Introductory Article" to the Book Revelation)

entries.title: Amos 9:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:8 Israel will be treated like all other nations that sin, except that YHWH will not totally destroy His people of promise (cf. Amos 5:4-7,14-15; 9:11-15). A righteous remnant of the house of Jacob will be spared! This theme is often repeated in Jeremiah.

  1. Judah will survive, Jer. 4:27; 5:10,18; 33:16
  2. Israel will survive, Jer. 30:11; 31:35-36

God's eternal plan of redemption (i.e. the Messiah for all peoples) depends on it!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "the eyes of the Lord God are on the sinful nation" This idiom, "the eyes of the Lord God," refers to His tender watchcare over His covenant people (i.e. Deut. 11:12). However, the addition of the phrase, "the sinful nation," shows the dilemma. Maybe the best way to express this is as a parent's pain at the poor life choices of a child (cf. Hosea 11). A truly loving parent must let the consequences of poor choices play out for the long term health, happiness, and maturity of the child, but it is very hurtful to both parties.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "destroy" This term (BDB 1029, KB 1552) is used three times in this verse. It means "to annihilate," "to destroy," "to terminate." This is such a contrast to the use of this same term in Deut. 33:26-29, where it refers to YHWH destroying His covenant people's enemies (i.e. Holy War).

Here, they are now the enemy (Hiphil PERFECT with waw). Yet even here there is a glimmer of hope, "I will not totally destroy the house of Jacob" (Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Hiphil IMPERFECT, a way to show intensity). Because of Amos 9:11 this could refer to Judah!

entries.title: Amos 9:9-10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:9-10 The Hebrew text is uncertain. Apparently this refers to some type of sifting process either for judgment (i.e. pebble) or for salvation (i.e. grain kernels). The context implies the righteous remnant will be spared and not one of them lost (i.e. Amos 9:9d). But for the wicked, YHWH will judge Israel like all other idolatrous nations (i.e. Amos 9:10).

The VERB "shake" (BDB 631, KB 681, Hiphil PERFECT with waw and Niphal PERFECT) refers to grain which is shaken through a sieve to remove the stones or dirt clods that may be mixed in with the heads of grain.

The word translated "kernel" (NASB, NJB, while NKJ has "the smallest grain") can also mean "pebble" (cf. 2 Sam. 17:13, KB 459; NRSV). This term (BDB 865) is usually translated "bundle," "parcel," "pouch," or "bag." Here it refers to an object caught in the bundling (reaping) process of stacking and tying grain stalks together in the field.

"Among all nations" probably relates to Amos 9:4, where YHWH sends judgment even on those sinful Israelites who are taken into exile. Even in other nations YHWH's judgment will destroy His faithless covenant people (cf. Amos 9:10b). There is no place to hide from God's wrath (cf. Amos 5:19; Jer. 23:24; Ps. 139:7-12).

entries.title: Amos 9:11 "In that day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:11 "In that day" This phrase appears several times (cf. Amos 2:16; 8:3,9,18). See note at Amos 2:16. Israel thought "that day" of YHWH's visitation would be a blessing, but Amos prophesied it would be a judgment (e.g. Amos 5:18-20). Now Amos reverses the prophecy. For the righteous remnant "that day" will be a restoration of the covenant promises to David (cf. 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17). In Amos 9:13-14 the promises of YHWH to Moses, especially Deut. 28:1-14, are emphasized.

It is crucial we see that the prophets of the OT always look back to the Mosaic covenant stipulations. Moses knew that the descendants of the Patriarchs could not keep the covenant (cf. Deut. 28:58-63; 29:25-28), as did Joshua (cf. Josh. 24:19; see Paul's view in Galatians 3).

However, Deuteronomy also holds out hope that a future day of forgiveness and restoration provided by YHWH will come (cf. Deut. 30:5) through His Messiah (cf. Deut. 18:18). It is this hope that the prophets pick up on and expand into an eschatological day of victory and abundance, not judgment!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: DAY (yom)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

▣ "the fallen booth of David" This idiom refers to the kingdom of David, symbolized in Jerusalem as its capital and spiritual center. The golden age of the United Monarchy (i.e. a godly king representing YHWH), with its prosperity, security, and religious faithfulness is restored.

The prediction of a coming Messiah always goes back to Judah (cf. Genesis 49; 2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17; Isa. 7:14; 9:6-7; 11:1-9; Jer. 33:15,17; Micah 4:1-5; 5:2-5a).

▣ "its breaches" Verse 11 is literally a reference to the walls of Jerusalem. It is FEMININE PLURAL (BDB 829), which may be a subtle way of referring to the reunification of Israel and Judah (i.e. one capital and worship center).

entries.title: Amos 9:11-15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:11-15 The paragraph division is uncertain (all paragraph divisions are opinions, not inspiration; there is no textual marker in Hebrew or Greek, except a repeated phrase or change of subject or speaker). The context shifts unexpectedly from judgment to restoration (and from Samaria to Jerusalem). This shift of subjects is common in the Prophets. However, the message of hope is sure (i.e. Amos 5:14-15)!

entries.title: Amos 9:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:12 This verse describes the military restoration to the limits of the Promised Land under David and Solomon. This eschatological promise takes on universal implications in Acts 15:16-17, where "Edom" (MT) is changed to "Adam" (i.e. mankind) in the Septuagint (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTAUGINT), which is quoted by James (also note Paul's use of Hosea 1:10; 2:23 in Rom. 9:24-26)! This universal theme is also reflected in Amos 9:5-6,7 (cf. Gen. 3:15; 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6; Isa. 42:1,4,6,10-11; 49:6; 51:4; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

This restoration to the Promised Land (e.g. Gen. 12:1-3; 13:14-17; 15:7) is in direct contrast to Amos 9:1-4, 9-10. YHWH's relation to Abraham and his seed was based on covenant obedience. If they did not:

  1. they would "be destroyed," Deut. 4:26; 6:15; Josh. 23:15; 1 Kgs. 13:34; Amos 9:8
  2. they would be "plucked from" the land, Deut. 28:63
  3. they would be "uprooted," Deut. 29:28; 1 Kgs. 14:15; 2 Chr. 7:20
  4. they would "perish," Josh. 23:13,16
  5. they would be "cut off," 1 Kgs. 9:7
  6. they would "be carried away," 2 Kgs. 17:6,23; 18:9-11; 25:21 (also 23:27)

But if they obeyed, then they would remain in the land, 2 Kgs. 18:12; 21:8; 2 Chr. 33:8 (cf. 2 Sam. 7:10).

So often in the Prophets, YHWH's people returning to "their own land" is emphasized (cf. Isa. 14:1-2; Jer. 16:15; Ezek. 11:17; 34:13,17; 36:24; 37:12,14,21; Amos 9:15).

▣ "when the plowman will overtake the reaper" Amos is apparently restating Lev. 26:5. Obedience to the covenant brings prosperity.

▣
NASB, Peshitta  "all the hills will be dissolved"
NKJV, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB  "all the hills shall flow with it"
NET  "it will flow down all the hillsides"
JPSOA  "all the hills shall wave
  [with grain]"
LXX  "the hills shall be thickly grown"

The VERB (BDB 556, KB 555, Hithpolel IMPERFECT) means "melt" (i.e. YHWH's judgment, cf. Micah 1:4; Nahum 1:5), but here it is a hyperbole of flowing grape juice by treading, a symbol of agricultural abundance (JPSOA, NET, LXX)!

entries.title: Amos 9:13-15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:13-15 The time element of this verse must be eschatological, for the descendants of Abraham will be subjugated again and again in history (i.e. Dan. 9:24-27). This promise (political peace and agricultural abundance, cf. Lev. 26:5, another eschatological text is Joel 3:18) is still conditional on covenant obedience. This is not specifically stated, but surely implied.

entries.title: Amos 9:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 9:14 This restoration is a reversal of Deut. 28:38-40; Amos 5:11; Micah 6:15; Zeph. 1:13. YHWH's people will plant vineyards in His land and enjoy their fruit (i.e. imagery for security and longevity in the land, e.g. Jer. 31:5; Ezek. 28:26; 1 Pet. 1:4-5).

entries.title: Amos 9:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
9:15 Even this seemingly unconditional promise must be evaluated in light of the history of the Jewish people. Obviously it has both an eschatological aspect (cf. 2 Sam. 7:10; Jer. 24:6; 32:41; 42:10) and a historical aspect.
